CVE-2026-121458 [MCP]: Instatic before 0.0.21 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in its AI/MCP content read tools that allows low-privileged authenticated users with ai.chat and content.edit.own capabilities to access data rows belonging to other users by calling content_get_document and content_list_documents without the object-level authorization checks enforced by the normal HTTP API. Attackers can use the MCP interface to retrieve private or unpublished draft content and enumerate rows from the posts system table, resulting in cross-user data disclosure.

CVE-2026-121419 [MCP]: SurrealDB from 3.1.0 before 3.3.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability where the MCP BoundSubject fingerprint uses the access method name instead of per-user identity for JWT/Bearer access. Attackers with a valid low-privilege token for the same access method and a victim's mcp-session-id can hijack the session and execute MCP tools with the victim's roles and permissions.

CVE-2026-76894 [MCP]: CKAN MCP Server is a tool for querying CKAN open data portals. Prior to 0.4.112, the DataStore table UI in src/resources/datastore-table-ui.ts accepts window message events without validating event.origin and sends JSON-RPC messages through postMessage with a wildcard target origin. A frame that can reach the embedded document can inject fabricated fields or records, spoof pending ui/initialize responses, disrupt the MCP UI handshake, or receive outbound messages when the resource is embedded by an untrusted parent. CVE-2026-88968 [Claude Code]: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool. Prior to 2.1.251, the Edit tool validates a target using pathname and symlink resolution that is not bound to the underlying directory inode or file descriptor. On macOS, attacker-controlled code running in the Bash sandbox can atomically replace an in-workspace parent directory with a symlink after validation, causing the unsandboxed Edit implementation to overwrite a user-writable file outside the workspace. 3.0.0CLI ## V3 by Default, Classic and Desktop App Retired This release makes V3 the default agent harness for interactive Kiro CLI sessions on hosts that can run it. Existing V2 users are asked before the default applies, and Kiro upgrades custom agents still in the V2 format unless you turn that off. Kiro CLI is now a single standalone kiro-cli binary that retires the Classic interface, the desktop app, and inline autocomplete. V3 brings capabilities V2 does not have. Cloud sessions let you disconnect and resume later from /sessions. Memory, once enabled, carries repository context forward.…
